source: Caucheteux, Gramfort, King (2021 preprint; 2023 Nat Hum Behav) Long-range and hierarchical language predictions in brains and algorithms
finding: Adding a window of future-word representations from GPT-2 to its activations improves how well it predicts fMRI. Fronto-parietal cortex fits deeper and more distant forecasts than temporal cortex.
numbers: N=304 subjects, 70 min of stories (Narratives set). Layer 8 of GPT-2. Peak brain score R=0.23 in superior temporal sulcus (60% of explainable signal). Best forecast distance 8 words. Brain-score gain 23% (+-9% across subjects). Angular gyrus vs Heschl depth k difference 2.5+-0.3, p<1e-12.
limits: Forecast is a linear add-on, not a causal test. Random forecast features gave no gain. Using GPT-2 generated words instead of true future words gave lower but similar results. Correlational fMRI.
agent_relevance: Gives a measured hint that useful prediction is multi-scale: near-term syntax, far-term semantics. A scaffold that plans at several horizons has this support. Background only.

source: Millidge, Tschantz, Buckley (2020) Predictive coding approximates backprop along arbitrary computation graphs
finding: Predictive coding with local rules converges to exact backprop gradients on any computation graph. Built PC CNN, RNN and LSTM that match backprop.
numbers: CNNs on SVHN, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, 5 seeds: performance largely indistinguishable from backprop. LSTM trained on next-character prediction on the full works of Shakespeare. PC cost about 100x backprop compute because inference must iterate.
limits: Exact equivalence needs initialised feedforward sweep and fixed-prediction assumption. Small models only. No language model at scale.
agent_relevance: The hierarchical error-flow story is mathematically a way to do backprop. It gives no new reasoning method. Background only.

source: Innocenti, Achour, Buckley (2025) muPC: scaling predictive coding to 100+ layer networks (NeurIPS 2025)
finding: Depth-muP parameterisation lets residual PC networks train stably up to 128 layers. Learning rates transfer zero-shot across width and depth.
numbers: Fully connected residual nets on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10. MNIST about 98% reached in 5 epochs, 5x faster than the previous benchmark. 128 layers max.
limits: Authors say it fixes only some pathologies. Simple tasks, CIFAR10 far from SOTA (fully connected). No transformer or language task.
agent_relevance: Shows the training-side limit: PC networks only just reached depth 100 on toy tasks, nowhere near LLM scale.

source: Goemaere, Oliviers, Bogacz, Demeester (2025-2026) ePC: fast and deep predictive coding in digital simulation
finding: Standard state-based PC suffers exponential signal decay with depth. An error-based reformulation (ePC) restores near-backprop accuracy and converges orders of magnitude faster.
numbers: Test accuracy, 5 seeds, MSE loss, ResNet-18 CIFAR-10: ePC 92.17+-0.26, sPC 53.74 (copied from Pinchetti), backprop 92.36+-0.12. CIFAR-100 top-1: ePC 68.52, backprop 69.94. VGG-7 CIFAR-10: ePC 88.98 vs sPC 77.79 vs BP 88.94.
limits: Image classification only. ResNet-18 sPC numbers copied from another paper because it was unstable. Authors' own claim of competitiveness.
agent_relevance: Depth failure of PC is partly an engineering artefact, not a theory failure. Does not touch LLM reasoning.

source: Pinchetti et al. (2025, ICLR) Benchmarking predictive coding networks made simple (PCX)
finding: First broad benchmark of PC networks on CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet. Models up to depth 7 are near backprop. Deeper ones lag. Best PC variants use nudging.
numbers: Table 1, test accuracy %: VGG-5 CIFAR-10 PC-CE 86.61 vs BP-CE 88.11. ResNet-18 CIFAR-10: PC-CE 43.19, best PC (iPC) 70.44, BP-CE 92.83. Tiny ImageNet ResNet-18 top-1: PC-CE 9.52 vs BP-CE 58.00; top-5: 26.21 vs 79.94.
limits: Vision only. Their stated trend: VGG5 > VGG7 > VGG9 > ResNet for PC, opposite for backprop. Table column alignment from PDF text; exact cell mapping for Tiny ImageNet rows should be rechecked.
agent_relevance: Independent negative evidence: hierarchical PC as a learning rule does not scale in depth. Do not rely on it for deep reasoning stacks.

source: Salvatori, Mali, Buckley, Lukasiewicz, Rao, Friston, Ororbia (2023-2025) Brain-inspired computational intelligence via predictive coding
finding: Survey of PC in ML. Says PC is competitive with backprop for 5-7 layer conv nets but degrades with depth, and that matching backprop on large language models is still open work.
numbers: Optimum inference iterations T between L and 2L for L layers. A PC with KL energy (categorical) lets PC transformers perform 'almost as well' as standard transformers (Pinchetti 2022).
limits: Authors are PC advocates. 'Almost as well' is not quantified in the survey.
agent_relevance: No PC-trained LLM of note as of 2025. The claim that PC is how LLMs should be built is unsupported.

source: van Zwol, Jefferson, van den Broek (2024-2026) Predictive coding networks and inference learning: tutorial and survey
finding: Tutorial says most PC work uses small MLPs or small CNNs, and variants remain slower than backprop. Notes softmax (categorical output) as the ingredient missing from standard PC for transformers.
numbers: Benchmark tables reproduce Pinchetti 2025 values. Cites Shain 2020 and Schrimpf 2021 as fMRI evidence for predictive processing in language.
limits: Only the language section and limits were read. Secondary source for brain-language claims.
agent_relevance: Same message: scale limits. Useful as a map of who did what.

source: Lotter, Kreiman, Cox (2017) Deep predictive coding networks for video prediction and unsupervised learning (PredNet)
finding: PredNet sends forward only prediction errors, with top-down predictions, on video. It beats a matched network that sends forward activations.
numbers: Rotating faces test: MSE 0.0152, SSIM 0.937 (PredNet L0) vs CNN-LSTM encoder-decoder 0.0180 / 0.907 vs copy-last-frame 0.125 / 0.631. PredNet Lall MSE 0.0157, SSIM 0.921. Also decodes steering angle on KITTI.
limits: Small gains over a control that shares the architecture. Video prediction only.
agent_relevance: Oldest working AI system built on the Rao-Ballard scheme. Shows the idea works for prediction, not for deliberate thinking.

source: Bhatt (2026) Predictive coding and information bottleneck for hallucination detection in LLMs (PCIB)
finding: Uses PC-motivated signals (surprise against context priors, context adherence, falsifiability) as features for a small hallucination detector. Beats heuristics, near big LLM judges on a tiny sample.
numbers: HaluBench subset N=200, balanced. Theory baseline AUROC 0.8017. Supervised base 0.8274; improved features 0.8669 (+4.95%). Lynx 70B 87.4% accuracy, GPT-4o 86.5%, RAGAS 66.9%. Simple averaging of signals AUROC 0.48. Negative result: rationalisation signal fails to separate hallucinations.
limits: Single author, N=200, one benchmark, no replication. Comparison mixes AUROC and accuracy. The link to PC is a naming of signals, not a test of PC.
agent_relevance: A cheap check (surprise against the stated context before answering) could be a gate in our schema. Weak evidence; an idea, not a result.

source: Ma et al. (2024) Non-myopic generation of language models for reasoning and planning (Predictive-Decoding)
finding: Not predictive coding by name. Model-predictive-control foresight: sample future steps, reweight the current step. Training-free.
numbers: Llama-3-8B: about 60% of examples myopic; 76.5% of GSM8K errors myopic vs 57.3% for correct. +7.2% on GSM8K, +25.3% on AlfWorld. Beats MCTS by 2.4% and guided decoding by 1.4% with about 50% of the FLOPs.
limits: Relies on LLM self-evaluation of foresight; step-score calibration error stayed high (0.332 to 0.323 on GSM8K with 3-step foresight). Control theory, included only as the nearest agent-loop analogue of predict-then-correct.
agent_relevance: Direct use of forecast-then-correct inside a decoding loop. Fits the Caucheteux finding that longer-range forecast helps. A pattern for operators that look ahead before committing.

source: Yang, He, Homan, Sommer, Staub, Hinzen (2026) Cross-lingual brain-language model alignment is robust but challenges hierarchical and computational accounts
finding: In three languages, transformer brain scores are stable across layers. Context-sensitive embeddings do not beat static FastText. Layer-wise surprisal does not reproduce the layer profile. Argues against prediction as the main reason LLMs match brains.
numbers: fMRI of a Little Prince audiobook: 49 English, 35 Mandarin, 28 French listeners. mBERT layer 12 vs FastText: BERT>FastText tests not significant (all p>0.95).
limits: BERT-class encoders, not GPT-scale. One book. Does not refute prediction in the brain, only the inference from brain score to computation.
agent_relevance: Strong caution: the claim that LLM depth maps onto cortical hierarchy is contested. Do not cite brain scores as support for layered thinking.

source: Kolbl et al. (2025) The predictive brain: neural correlates of word expectancy align with LLM prediction probabilities
finding: BERT predictability of nouns tracks brain signals: higher predictability gives lower N400 and more pre-onset activity in EEG and MEG during audiobook listening.
numbers: N=29 participants, simultaneous EEG and MEG. N400 windows 300-450 ms (EEG), 500-650 ms (MEG). Pre-activation vs N400: EEG r2=0.56, p=0.0126; MEG r2=0.35, p=0.0708 (not significant). Replication subsets: EEG second subset p=0.11, third p<0.05.
limits: Small N. MEG effects weaker. Predictability from BERT (bidirectional), not a causal model of what the listener knew.
agent_relevance: LLM probability is a usable proxy for human surprise. A model surprise score can stand in for prediction error in a loop.

source: Rao, Sathish, Jiang, Bryan, Rangarajan (2025) Lessons from neuroscience for AI
finding: Argues next-token loss is a form of predictive coding but LLMs lack three parts of full PC models: action-coupled generative models, hierarchical compositional structure and episodic memory.
numbers: Position paper; no benchmark numbers.
limits: Perspective by a co-founder of the theory, not a test. No measured LLM results.
agent_relevance: Names the things our schema adds from outside the model: actions, hierarchy, memory. Design argument only.

source: Xie (2026) LPC-SM: local predictive coding and sparse memory for long-context language modeling
finding: Hybrid 158M model with a predictive-correction block. In ablation, removing the predictive coding part did not hurt base LM loss.
numbers: Stage A final LM loss: full 12.630; without predictive coding 12.413 (-1.7%, better); without slow memory 12.671; without mHC 15.127 (+19.8%). Stage C at 4096 tokens: delayed-identifier key cross-entropy 14.396 to 12.031.
limits: Single independent author, heavily undertrained model (loss above 12), no strong baseline. Author warns against reading ablations as verdicts.
agent_relevance: Null result: a PC block added no clear gain in loss. Do not expect PC modules to improve an LLM cheaply.

source: Morrill, Zemel (2026) DeltaNet-PC: test-time memory without backpropagation through time
finding: PC-native associative memory for sequences, linked to DeltaNet linear attention. Perfect recall when memory size matches length.
numbers: 100% recall up to L=D=1,024 (3 seeds). 99.99% test accuracy at full memory load L=256. 100% key-value recall with as few as 32 training examples.
limits: Synthetic recall tasks only. Authors claim no accuracy advantage over linear attention; the gain is locality and memory footprint.
agent_relevance: PC as a memory write rule (update by prediction error). Memory analogue: store what is not already predicted.

source: Potter, Rhodes (2026) Learning long-range dependencies with temporal predictive coding (tPC-RTRL)
finding: Temporal PC with real-time recurrent learning recovers BPTT gradients under assumptions, with near-identical results on language and translation.
numbers: WikiText-103 byte-level validation 1.865 vs 1.864 BPC (tPC-RTRL vs BPTT). English-French CCMatrix subset 20.23 vs 20.29 BLEU. Nanodrone: reusing inference at deployment halves position error, 0.402 m vs 0.805 m open loop.
limits: Small recurrent models, not transformers. Equivalence under explicit assumptions. Only the abstract was read.
agent_relevance: Closest to a working PC language model: parity with BPTT at small scale. Deployment-time iterative inference that folds in observations is the agent-loop idea (correct a rollout with observed state).

source: Innocenti (2025) Towards scaling deep neural networks with predictive coding: theory and practice (PhD thesis)
finding: States that PC's claimed advantages over backprop, such as faster training, have not been consistently observed and that deep PC nets remain practically untrainable. Shows PC learning acts like an approximate second-order trust-region method.
numbers: Abstract and introduction only; thesis is very long.
limits: Opened abstract and headings, not all chapters.
agent_relevance: Reliable statement of the field's open problem by a leading practitioner.

source: Murphy (2024) Shadow of the (hierarchical) tree: reconciling symbolic and predictive components of the neural code for syntax
finding: Argues language models and predictive mechanisms explain linear, horizontal syntax but little of hierarchical compositional structure. Proposes a hybrid neurosymbolic model.
numbers: Discussion paper; no new experiment or numbers.
limits: Opinion; 11.6k words. Read abstract and introduction.
agent_relevance: Supports adding explicit structure (our states and operators) on top of next-token prediction.

source: arXiv search 'predictive coding' + 'language model' (retrieved 2026-11-17)
finding: The PC-and-LLM literature is small and mostly 2025-2026: hallucination detection, long-context architectures, PC memory, brain-alignment studies. No paper found that runs a full PC loop inside an LLM agent.
numbers: 42 of 50 results read. Relevant: 2601.15652, 2604.03263, 2610.15185, 2602.18131, 2605.21049, 2506.08511. Not opened: 2608.12398 (energy-based hierarchical model), 2604.00886 (PixelPrune).
limits: A listing, not a study. Absence of results is weak evidence.
agent_relevance: The gap itself: nobody has measured PC-style loops for LLM reasoning, so claims here are open.

source: Heilbron et al. (2022) A hierarchy of linguistic predictions during natural language comprehension (PNAS)
finding: Reported evidence that predictions at several linguistic levels each add to brain responses beyond word surprisal.
numbers: Not verified this session: page returned HTTP 403.
limits: Cited from memory; numbers not checked.
agent_relevance: Hierarchy-of-prediction evidence in humans; unverified until opened.

source: Caucheteux, Gramfort, King (2023) Evidence of a predictive coding hierarchy in the human brain listening to speech (Nature Human Behaviour)
finding: Journal version of the 2021 preprint (c01). Nature page redirected to a login.
numbers: Not verified; use c01 numbers only.
limits: Final numbers may differ from the preprint.
agent_relevance: Same as c01.

source: Song et al. (2024) Inferring neural activity before plasticity as a foundation for learning beyond backpropagation (Nat Neurosci)
finding: Prospective configuration: infer target activity first, then change weights. Cited by ePC as reducing interference in online and continual learning.
numbers: Not opened. Claim relayed in ePC text (c04).
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Order of operations (infer first, then update) matches a scaffold that reasons before committing to memory.

source: Pinchetti et al. (2022) Predictive coding beyond Gaussian distributions (NeurIPS)
finding: Generalised PC energy to KL form; used for PC transformers said to perform 'almost as well' as backprop transformers (per survey c06).
numbers: Not opened; no figures verified; URL is a placeholder.
limits: Second-hand through c06.
agent_relevance: Only PC-trained transformer in the record; scale small.

source: Whittington, Bogacz (2017) An approximation of the error backpropagation algorithm in a predictive coding network with local Hebbian synaptic plasticity
finding: Showed PC with local Hebbian rules approximates backprop on MLPs; the foundation for c02.
numbers: Not opened; relayed in Millidge 2020 text (c02).
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Background only.

source: Barenholtz (2025) Predicting the demise of predictive coding (Substack essay)
finding: Argues predictive coding is a mismatch for generative models like LLMs, since LLMs do not predict in the sense the theory means.
numbers: Only a search snippet seen; no numbers.
limits: Blog essay, opinion.
agent_relevance: Competing view to record; not evidence.
